faq: What does this tool calculate?
Miles from kilometres, at the exact conversion factor — route distances in particular, though any length converts identically.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes, in your browser as you type. No account, nothing uploaded.
How accurate is the result?
Exact to the factor. A kilometre is defined through the metre, as is the mile, so the conversion carries no approximation.
Does the route include live traffic?
No — this is unit conversion, not routing. Traffic belongs to the journey, not to its units.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Unrelated to conversion, happily: both numbers describe the same road once converted. Convert the road distance you measured.
A quick mental shortcut?
Multiply by 0.6 for a rough idea, then by 1.036 for the truth — or just use this page and skip the folklore.
The reverse conversion?
Miles × 1.609344 — the Miles to Kilometers Route Converter is organised for that direction.
Speed limits: 130 km/h in mph?
130 × 0.621371 = 80.8 mph — the conversion that keeps a US driver legal and unsurprised on the autoroute.
Odometer in km, fuel in gallons — mixed logs?
Convert the distance here, then the Gallons Needed tool takes over with miles and mpg. One conversion, at the seam, keeps the log clean.
Is a kilometre exactly 0.621371 miles?
To six figures, yes — 0.6213711922 in full. The definitions leave no wobble.
